events.text: Torrential rainfall the began just before the morning commute would soon add up to notable flash flooding across Weslaco, parts of Mercedes, and extending westward to the east side of Donna and southward to near US 281 (Progreso). Rainfall totals of near 7 inches were recorded along IH-2 near the Mid-Valley Airport, in just over two hours. Flash flooding included numerous streets, including the frontage road, with 2-3 feet of water as well as several properties with water incursion into them. Some of the reports included: *Numerous social media reports and news media coverage of flooding along the I-2 frontage road in Weslaco near North Republic St and North Texas Blvd. *The IH-2 f…
The public reported a large tree limb down near Lincoln and Nebraska Roads in San Juan, TX.
The ASOS at McAllen/Miller International Airport (KMFE) measured a wind gusts of 54 knots or 62 mph.

Observations from several locations in southern Hidalgo County recorded a shorter-lived freeze event (than on the prior morning), with minimum temperatures ranging from 28 to 31F in most areas. Duration of freezing temperatures (32F or lower) was around 2.5 to 3.5 hours.
Cold Weather Advisory Criteria (Wind chills at or below 30F) was reached at Edinburg International Airport for 9 hours from 11:35pm CST on January 26th to 8:35am CST on Tuesday January 27th.

Edinburg International Airport recorded freezing temperatures (32F degrees or lower) for 9 hours from 11:35pm CST on January 26th to 8:35am CST on Tuesday January 27th. A Hard Freeze (temperatures at or below 27F degrees) occurred for over 3.5 hours from 4:15-7:55am CST January 27th.
Extreme Cold Warning Criteria (temperatures at or below 20F degrees) was reached at Edinburg International Airport for 4 hours from 5:15-9:15am CST Monday January 26th.
Extreme Cold Warning Criteria (temperatures at or below 20F degrees) was reached at Weslaco/Mid Valley Airport for 4 hours from 5:15-9:15am CST on Monday January 26th.

A combination of observing platforms in southern Hidalgo County (City of Edinburg, McAllen, Mission, Weslaco, etc) recorded minimum temperatures in the upper 20s on January 26th. Freezing (32F or lower) temperatures arrived around 4 AM, and continued through around 930 AM before sunshine rapidly warmed temperatures above freezing. An unknown amount of minor damage was likely to winter crops, mainly due to the sharp temperature change from prior to the freeze until after it.

Edinburg International Airport recorded freezing temperatures (32F degrees or lower) for 11 hours from 9:55pm on January 25th to 9:35am CST on Monday January 26th. A Hard Freeze (temperatures at or below 27F degrees) occurred for over 3.5 hours from 4:15-7:55am CST January 26th. Minimum temperatures were in the low to mid 20s.
McAllen/Miller International Airport (MFE) recorded minimum wind chill values at or below 30F degrees (Cold Weather Advisory Criteria) for 2.5 hours from 6:25-9:10am CST on Sunday January 25th.
Edinburg International Airport recorded minimum wind chill values at or below 30F degrees (Cold Weather Advisory Criteria) for 9 hours from 1:15-10:15am CST on the morning of Sunday January 25th.

Local broadcast media (KRGV Channel 5 News) provided video and still photos of street flooding in Weslaco, with 1 to 2 feet of water depth (estimated). Rainfall of 2.4 fell with a cluster of storms, including more than 2 inches in 90 minutes, at the Mid Valley Airport in Weslaco. Similar rainfall totals were estimated in urban/poor drainage locations west to Pharr.
Weslaco Emergency Management reported a residence trailer rolled over during strong winds just north of the expressway near Mile 10 and Mile 4 1/2 West with no injuries.

The San Antonio Express-News reported, via video reports on social media, urban flooding with water depths up to 2 feet in streets across portions of the McAllen metropolitan region during the early to mid evening. Rainfall totals ranged from 2.5 to nearly 3 inches, much which fell within 90 to 120 minutes. Damage to vehicles was unknown, though several had water levels halfway to two-thirds the way up their tire heights.
Video (via Facebook) showing numerous homes and structures with minor damage in south Donna. A stop sign was reported to be blown over.
Weslaco Mid-Valley Airport (AWOS) recorded a peak wind gust of 58 mph.
A NWS Employee reported metal roofing structures and a fence blown over near the intersection of Benito Ramirez and Terry Road in Edinburg, TX.

Just after 740 PM CDT on June 12, 2025, a strong microburst descended from a severe thunderstorm in North Alamo, near the city line with Muniz, causing damage to traffic lights, a stand alone tower, powerlines/poles, fences and trees as well as ripped off the roof of a house, flipped a trailer and dislocated a metal structure. Altogether, the damage locations were along a northwest to southeast oriented line with six of the seven surveyed locations north of Expressway 83/east of Interstate 69C (beginning near the Muniz/North Alamo city line) and the 7th spot of Expressway 83 in Donna. For most of the damage path, estimated wind speeds ranged from 75 to 85 mph. Detailed damage along…
Hidalgo County Fire Marshal reported at least two large trees blown down, including on the road along FM 2825 near the intersections of Sunshine and Val Verde Road.
Hidalgo County Fire Marshal reported a power pole leaning along FM 490 just west of US 281/IH-69C.
A member of the public reported 1.5 inch hail via Facebook, about 1 mile east of Progreso near the international border.
A trained spotter reported golf ball size hail just northeast of Donna, TX.
A member of the public reported 3 inch diameter (tea cup size) hail, via Facebook. The stone was oblong shape, with a width of 1.5 inches.
A trained weather spotter reported golf ball size hail near the intersection of Wisconsin and Veterans in south Edinburg.
A member of the public reported golf ball size hail in north McAllen (via Facebook) near the Edinburg city line.

There was a photo received from DHR Health of 2 inch size hail that fell near Dove and McColl along the Edinburg/McAllen line. Within a half mile of this location, a member of the public provided a photo via Facebook, also showing 2 inch diameter hail.
A member of the public sent photos through Facebook showing approximately golf ball sized hail.
A member of the public reported one inch size hail in north Pharr near the McAllen city line.
A member of the public reported 2 inch hail via Facebook in north McAllen.
A member of the public posted a Facebook photo of golf ball sized hail.
A member of the public posted a photo on Facebook of 1 inch hail.
A local EM reported ping pong size hail at his residence in north McAllen.
There was a report received from a HAM Operator of 1 inch hail. The hail lasted for ten minutes at this location.

Just after 7 PM CDT May 8, 2025, a strong microburst descended from a hail-producing supercell thunderstorm in North McAllen, near the city line with Edinburg. Damage, mainly to over 100 large mesquite and live oak tree limbs, occurred between north Taylor Road and north Ware Road. Along and just north of Mile 8 1/2 Road, one unanchored recreational vehicle (RV) was flipped, with several sections of fence blown down and small portions of the roof removed. Along Ware Road, one industrial business lost its sheet metal roof and garage. The most notable damage was seen east of Ware Road, mainly between Mile 9 Road and State Road (SR) 107. In the El Pacifico neighborhood, one residence…
An emergency manager reported 500 acres of corn destroyed in a farm field about 4.4 miles west-southwest of McCook.
Broadcast media shared a resident report of estimated 1 inch hail in Weslaco. Time estimated based on radar data.
Broadcast media shared a video from a resident with estimated quarter size hail at the intersection of Mile 9 and 1015 north of Weslaco.

The Texas Department of Transportation, along with local law enforcement, the public, and emergency management, reported high standing water of 2 to 3 feet in several poor drainage locations of southeastern Hidalgo County that persisted for two more days following historic seasonal rainfall/rainfall rates. This included much of the IH-2 frontage road from east Alamo through the Cameron County line (Mercedes/La Feria), as well as several Farm-to-Market roads which remained impassible for all or part of this time. Overwhelmed drainage systems took time for the water to run out completely, and the Flood Control Project (Main and North Floodways in southeastern Hidalgo County between W…

The Texas Department of Transportation, along with local law enforcement and the public, noted a continuation of high water along the IH-2 frontage roads between Mission and Alamo from just before midnight (standard time) on March 27th through mid to late afternoon on the 28th, as water was slow but steady to drain out of the area despite fair weather for most of the period.

Torrential rains that previously affected the McAllen/Edinburg metro area reached southeast Hidalgo County, from south of Weslaco to Edcouch and east to the Hidalgo/Cameron line, then south along the Mercedes/La Feria line and all the way to between Progreso and just west of Santa Maria. Similar to the situation in the Donna-Weslaco area, the IH-2 frontage road was littered with flooded vehicles, with rescued vehicles along the side of the elevated expressway. An estimated 3 or more feet of water was on the frontage roads. The rain in this area came in multiple rounds. A first round occurred between 430 and 6 PM, with additional rounds between 7 and 8 PM and again fro 930 to around…

Torrential rains moved out from the McAllen/metro into the mid-Valley section of Hidalgo County, to include locations east of Edinburg, including Elsa/Edcouch, then south through San Juan, Alamo, and Donna, extending south to around Military Highway (US 281) east of Pharr and near the Rio Grande. Poor drainage locations flooded with at least 3 feet of water depth, and nearly the entire IH-2 frontage road had 2 to 3 or more feet of water depth, with dozens of vehicles stranded and at least one hundred more removed from the floodwaters. A number of farm-to-market and state highways had pockets of flood waters, forcing closures that lasted into March 28th. In this flood area, there we…

A small tornado briefly touched down about 1.5 miles east of Edcouch, lifting the sheet metal roof of a warehouse belonging to a crop dusting company. Pieces of the roof were blown to the northeast along the 0.25 mile path, landing in open fields on the north and south side of SH-107. The debris was scattered in varying directions along the path. Partial metal wall failure was also noted to the building, which was a total loss. A metal building structure (MBS) hangar that sheltered one of the crop-dusting aircraft was also damaged, with a small portion of the roof lifted off and the garage door bent inward, toward the center of the circulation. The aircraft inside was also impacted…

Significant to locally devastating flash flooding began in the McAllen/Mission metropolitan area during mid-afternoon. Rainfall rates of at least 3 in 30 minutes were too much for the city's drainage infrastructure to handle, and soon after, city fire/rescue/police reported more than two dozen roads closed citywide and up to forty homes with an unknown amount of water depth inside, to the Emergency Management Coordinator. It was likely that several hundred homes had incident flooding, from affected to major damage - most concentrated in the south side of the city. The frontage roads on IH2 (Mission/McAllen) and IH-69C (Pharr/Edinburg) flooded with varying amounts of water, and hund…
Several trees were reported down and power outages in the town of Penitas.

McAllen ASOS recorded about 29 hours of wind chills at or below 30F degrees from 1:55am-11:55am on February 20th, from 11:25pm on February 20th to 1:16pm on February 21st, and from 2:40am to 8:40am on February 22. A minimum wind chill temperature between 25-27F degrees occurred on February 20th. Weslaco (Mid Valley Airport) AWOS site recorded about 46.5 hours of wind chills at or below 30F degrees from 12:55am-11:35am on February 20th and from 11:15pm on February 20th to 11:15am on February 22nd. A minimum wind chill temperature between 23-26F degrees occurred on February 20th.

Edinburg AWOS recorded about 46.5 hours of wind chills at or below 30F degrees from 11:35pm on February 19th to 12:15pm on February 20th, from 11:15pm on February 20th to 11:15pm on February 21st, and from 1:15am to 10:35am on February 22. A minimum wind chill temperature between 23-25F degrees occurred on February 20th. Texas Agriscience AWOS recorded about 52 hours of wind chills at or below 30F degrees from 10:15pm on February 19th to 12:15pm on February 20th and from 10:40pm on February 20th to 1:05pm on February 22nd. Minimum wind chill temperatures between 21-22F degrees occurred on February 20th.

McAllen recorded about 24 hours of freezing temperatures (32 degrees or lower) from 8:45pm January 21 to 8:50pm January 22, 2025. A minimum temperature between 26-27F degrees occurred between 2:53am to 3:53am on January 22.

We received a report from Amateur (HAM) Radio of ice on trees in Edinburg. We received a report from the public of a glazing of ice at FM 107 and Sugar Rd in Edinburg. There was also a report of ice glazing on cars in La Joya. Finally, we received a report from a CO-OP Observer of a light glaze on the rain gauge and trees in San Manuel. With temperatures at or below 32F degrees, it's likely that freezing rain was falling between 2:35am-7:55am on January 21.

South Texas International Airport in Edinburg recorded a total of 22 hours of freezing temperatures (32 degrees or lower) from 1:55am to 10:35am on January 21 and then again from 7:35pm on January 21 to 8:55am on January 22. on January 15, 2024. A minimum temperature of 25F degrees occurred between 6:15am and 7:55am on January 22.
McAllen recorded wind chills at or below 30F degrees for 8 hours from 10:53pm January 20 to 7:00am January 21. Minimum wind chills between 22-24F occurred between 12:53am to 9:53am on January 21.

South Texas International Airport in Edinburg recorded 31 hours (from 10:35am on January 20 to 6:35pm on January 21) of wind chills at or below 30F degrees (cold weather advisory wind chills). Within that time period, Edinburg International Airport recorded 8.5 hours (from 1:55am to 10:35am on January 21) of wind chills at or below 20F degrees (extreme cold advisory levels). A minimum wind chill value of 18F degrees occurred at times between 2:15am and 9:55am on January 21. Linn San Manuel recorded 16 hours (from 10:46pm on January 20 to 2:46pm on January 21) of wind chills at or below 30F degrees (cold weather advisory wind chills). A minimum wind chill value of 24F degrees occurr…

A pocket of torrential rainfall from a nearly stationary isolated thunderstorm, with measured and estimated rainfall between 3 and 4 inches in a very small area around downtown Edinburg, left 3 feet of water in roads around the Courthouse building, some of which entered structures of estimated depths of 1 to 1.5 feet. Damage was unknown at the time of this writing.
A landspout was reported in Donna. Image was shared on Slack/NWS Chat 2.0. Timing was based off their observation along with radar.

A small business La Michoacana Paletria y Neveria had visible damage to the exterior wall and roofing. A submitted photo of the damage was later confirmed by the broadcast media and emergency management. Winds estimated from similar damage to poor to fair construction in past events in the Rio Grande Valley. Other minor damage occurred at Mission Fire Station 4, where the bottom of a garage was peeled back.
Emergency Management reported trees down in Mission, Texas near Solar and Francisco.
A few golf ball size hail stones were observed.
Quarter to ping pong size hail was reported near the intersection of McColl and Military Highway...US 281.
A former COOP Observer reported quarter size hail briefly covering the ground just south of the intersection of 7 mile and North Doffing Road in Citrus City.
Nickel size hail was reported in the Citrus City area near/along the West 7 Mile Road.
Quarter size hail was reported near the intersection of Tom Gil and 3 Mile Line Road.
Quarter size hail briefly covered the ground in the vicinity of Doffing Road and Conway Avenue north of Mission.
Video showed quarter size hail near the intersection of La Homa Road and Mile 7 Road north of Mission.
Video showed hail dominant precipitation along P.J. Garza Road near Expressway 83.
Golfball size hail was reported along FM 490 near Faysville.
Golfball size hail was reported around 2 miles north of McCook by the public.
Baseball size hail was reported between 2 and 3 miles southeast of McCook. No damage was reported at the time.
Quarter size hail was reported.

A few sites in Northern Hildago County including Deep South Texas International Airport in Edinburg, Linn San Manuel, and CRN recorded temperatures at or below freezing for roughly 10-12 hours (between 8:46 PM on the 16th and 925 AM on the 17th). A Hard Freeze (temperatures below 28 degrees for 2 or more hours) at these sites in Northern Hildago County from anywhere between 5 and 10 hours. Linn San Manuel observed Hard Freeze conditions for 9.5 hours. Minimum temperature between 21F-22F was recorded between 446 AM and 755 AM on the 17th.

A few sites in Southern Hildago County including McAllen, Weslaco, Santa Ana, and Agriscience recorded temperatures at or below freezing for roughly 5-12 hours (between 7:45 PM on the 16th and 855 AM on the 17th). A Hard Freeze (temperatures below 28 degrees for 2 or more hours) at these sites in Southern Hildago County for up to 7 hours. Santa Ana was one site that observed Hard Freeze conditions for 7 hours. Minimum temperature between 21F-27F was recorded between 345 AM and 455 AM on the 17th.

A Minimum Wind Chill value of 11F degrees was recorded at the Deep South Texas International Airport (STX) in Edinburg at 3:35 AM. The duration of temperatures within the wind chill criteria was for about 10.5 hours.

A Minimum Wind Chill value of 13F degrees was recorded in McAllen and Weslaco at 5:35 AM and 4:55 AM, respectively. The duration of temperatures within the wind chill criteria lasted between 9-11 hours.

Multiple sites in southern Hildago County recorded temperatures at or below freezing between 8-11 hours (spanning between 1205 AM and 1115 AM on the 16th. This included McAllen, Weslaco, Santa Ana, and Agriscience. A Hard Freeze (temperatures below 28 degrees for 2 or more hours) occurred between the hours of 310 AM and 750 AM. Minimum temperatures fell between 26.9F and 28F degrees across the area. McAllen (record since 1942) set a new daily record (28F), breaking the prior record of 31F set in 2018.

Multiple sites in northern Hildago County recorded temperatures at or below freezing for 11-12 hours (spanning between 11 PM on the 15th and 1105 AM on the 16th. his included CRN, Linn San Manuel, and South Texas International Airport in Edinburg. A Hard Freeze (temperatures below 28 degrees for 2 or more hours) was also observed at a couple of these sites (South Texas International Airport in Edinburg and CRN) between the hours of 255 AM and 855 AM. Minimum temperatures fell between 27F and 28F degrees across the area.

A Minimum Wind Chill of 18F and 20F degrees was recorded in Weslaco and McAllen, at 9:55 AM and 10:10 AM, respectively. The duration of the wind chill criteria was less than a half hour at McAllen and for almost 4 hours at Weslaco.

Weslaco recorded 5 hours of freezing temperatures (32 degrees or lower) from 755AM to 1245PM on January 15, 2024. A minimum temperature of 31F degrees occurred between 855AM and 1135AM. Santa Ana recorded an hour of freezing temperatures (32 degrees or lower) from 845AM to 945AM on January 15, 2024. A minimum temperature of 32F degrees occurred at 845AM. McAllen recorded 2 hours of freezing temperatures (32 degrees or lower) from 930AM to 1130AM on January 15, 2024. A minimum temperature of 32F degrees occurred between 930AM and 1130AM. Agriscience recorded 6 hours of freezing temperatures (32 degrees or lower) from 7AM to 1PM on January 15, 2024. A minimum temperature of 29.5F deg…
A Minimum Wind Chill of 17F degrees was recorded at South Texas International (EBG) in Edinburg at 9:35 AM. The duration of the wind chill criteria was for about 4 and a half hours.

South Texas International Airport in Edinburg recorded a little bit over 6 hours of freezing temperatures (32 degrees or lower) from 635AM to 1255PM on January 15, 2024. A minimum temperature of 30F degrees occurred between 730AM and Noon. Linn San Manuel recorded 6 and a half hours of freezing temperatures (32 degrees or lower) from 615AM to 1246PM on January 15, 2024. A minimum temperature of 29F degrees occurred between 646AM and 1246PM. CRN recorded between 7-8 hours of freezing temperatures (32 degrees or lower) from 625AM to 1315PM on January 15, 2024. A minimum temperature of 29F degrees occurred between 920AM and 11 AM. A new daily record was set at San Manuel, with 28 degrees F.

A member of the public shared video of a landspout just east of La Villa. This landspout formed along the leading edge of an outflow boundary that raced through the Lower Rio Grande Valley the afternoon of September 16th. According to the member of the public who shared video of the event, it only last a minute or so and didn't appear to cause any damage as it was near the levee just east of La Villa.
Pictures from social media shows a metal structure crumpled up and blown several yards into the field across the street. Timing estimated by radar.
Pictures from social media show awning/roof damage to The End of the Trail Sports Bar #1 along FM493.
Pictures from social media show a large tree down in the backyard of a house across the street from Rick & Ron's Auto Sales. Minor roof damage was noted by the owner.
A member of the public recorded a video showing quarter sized hail and gusty winds at a self car wash at the intersection of Canton and Raul Longoria.
Members of the public reported 2 hail in Hidalgo. There were also reports of several cars with windshields either damaged or shattered due to the hail. Time estimated by radar.
Local media received pictures of hail estimated to be the size of hen egg near Granjeno, TX. Time estimated by radar.
A member of the public called to report dime and nickel sized hail. Time estimated on the time of the call and radar.

An NWS Storm Survey in southeastern Hidalgo County found metal roofs, large tree branches snapped, the top of a small palm tree snapped off and flung several yards, numerous power poles downed and a destroyed mobile home along Mile 3 Rd N between FM491 and Mile 2 E.
The ASOS station at the Mid Valley Airport (KTXW) recorded a wind gust of 50 knots at 12:55AM CDT.

A member of the public shared several pictures from the Progreso Port of Entry area showing damage to several grain silos and apparatus on the top of the silos. A few pictures in particular show a grain silo caved in. One limiting factor from going higher is the lack of damage to nearby mobile office structures in the foreground.

An NWS Storm Survey found some metal roof damage to Dorothy Thompson Middle School in Progreso. Additional damage was found in and around the town of Progreso, including several large tree branches down and a large tree partially uprooted at the corner of Creager Road and S Mile 2 W on the southeast side of Progreso. There was also significant damage to the roof of a large metal warehouse just east of the intersection of Creager Road and S Mile 2 W.

An NWS Storm Survey found damage to a large, corrugated light steel fence that was blown down along S FM493 a few miles south of Donna. There were several other areas of damage between there and the intersection of Calle Santiago and Creager Road. That damage included a low masonry wall of about 4 feet in height blown over at intersection of Midway Road and W 34th St; and several buildings, including homes, with partial loss of the roof of vinyl/metal siding along S Texas Blvd on the west side of Progreso.

The Fire Chief for Weslaco called and reported several business signs either damaged or blown down along Business 83. The largest sign blown down was an 8 foot tall Long John Silvers sign. An NWS Survey found there to be rust at the bottom of the sign, which kept wind estimates from being higher.
An official NWS Survey found several sections of netting ripped at the Topgolf in Pharr. Timing estimated by radar.

An NWS Storm Survey in and around the McAllen-Miller International Airport found a Cessna had been flipped onto its roof and a Gulfstream jet turned and pushed into the grass by strong thunderstorm winds. The McAllen-Miller International Airport ASOS (KMFE) officially recorded a wind gust of 74 mph before losing power. Wind estimates were closer to 74 knots, or 85 mph, due to the flipping of the Cessna. Additional damage was found downstream, or east, of the airport with large oak tree branches having been snapped and one oak tree snapped near its base at the McAllen Country Club. The roof of the Radisson Hotel McAllen Airport (0.5-1 mile east-southeast of the airport) was partiall…

The canopy over the gas pumps at the Exxon Gas station at the corner of Lark and N 23rd Street was blown over and pushed partially across the road. An official NWS Storm Survey team looked at the poles to the canopy and found that several of them had rust, which led to a slightly lower wind rating. Timing based on radar.
Member of the public shared an image of the roof blown off the Car Check Auto Service and Ultimate Dental Care building at the corner of N Cage Blvd and W Clark Ave. Timing estimated by radar.

An NWS Storm Survey found extensive damage along W Business 83 in McAllen. A poorly constructed roof and cinderblock wall with no bond beam caused a portion of the roof to collapse; the wall was about 35 feet high and fully exposed. A decently constructed metal roof system was partially torn off along with a garage door partially caved in at the intersection of N 22nd St and Beech Ave. The Linares Auto Center sign was also blown over at the corner of Business 83 and S 21st Street. The sign was mounted in concrete with some rust. It also fell on at least 3 cars in the parking lot. The strongest wind indicator was along S 20th St just south of Business 83 where wooden poles were bent…

An NWS Storm Survey found more than 50 percent of shingles off on a two story building with full exposure to the west-northwest along S 29th St in McAllen. To the southeast of there, a tin roof and over a dozen trusses and rafters were taken off a lumber store and blown across the road. Additionally, the parapet roof over the Ross Department store was partially blown off. The roof was approximately 50 feet off the ground.

An NWS Storm Survey found a McAllen Public Works truck impaled with 2x4s that were lofted into the front passengers side near the intersection of Nolana Ave W and N Bensten Road. The 2x4s was pulled from a weakly constructed wood scaffold nearby. Additional reports of semi-trucks turned over were reported by the broadcast media in the Walmart parking a few blocks east along Nolana Loop. Additional damage was found along N 23rd St with columns, which were rusted, of a gas station canopy bent near the base at the corner of N 23rd Street and Daffodil Ave. There was also minor metal damage to the roof of an abandoned car wash along N 23rd St across from McAllen High School.

An NWS Storm Survey found roofing material still in plastic along with pull back of cinder block cladding near the intersection of S Bryan Road and W Frontage Road. A little ways east, a large billboard and pole fell onto vehicles. Pole was anchored into dirt, but sitting on high water from recent rains and uprooted. Lower wind speeds used based on poor anchoring and lack of surrounding damage.
Several citizens reported several large trees and traffic signs down along with stop signs pulled out of the ground along Highway 495 and Sugar Road. Timing estimated by radar.
Weslaco Fire Marshal reported damage to four to five trees in his neighborhood in Mission.
Member of the public called in to report several trees that were uprooted along with several others that lost tree limbs. Timing based on their report and radar.
Member of the public shared pictures of damage to several large oak trees, including several large branches about 8 to 12 inches in diameter, that had snapped. Timing estimated by radar.

The ASOS station at McAllen-Miller International Airport observed winds equaling or exceeding 50 knots between 12:20AM CDT and 12:40AM CDT before briefly losing power shortly thereafter. The strongest wind gust of 64 knots was recorded at 12:34AM CDT. There was significant damage in and around the airport, including a Cessna that had been flipped and a Gulfstream aircraft that had been moved. Damage at the airport is listed in a later report from the NWS Storm Survey.
Broadcast media shared a picture of a few food trucks and trailers flipped over near the intersection of Bryan Road and Business 83 near Mission City Hall. Time estimated by radar.

A member of the public shared pictures of the Burger King in Palmview with its windows blown out around the play area. It's located at the intersection of Frontage Road and La Homa Road. Timing estimated from radar.

A member of the public shared pictures with an NWS employee of significant damage to a mobile home trailer. The pictures show the mobile home destroyed with only one wall still standing. Timing estimated by radar.
Video from the public shows the metal roof of a carport peeled back near the intersection of Mile 3 Road and Tom Gill Road. Time estimated by radar.
Member of the publics shows several mesquite trees down along Garza Avenue north of Military road. Time estimated by radar.
Video shared by a member of the public shows several large trees down along El Pinto Road near Rosendo Benavides Elementary School. Time estimated by radar.
The McAllen-Miller International Airport (KMFE) ASOS recorded a wind gust of 59 knots, or 68 mph, at 1:02PM CDT.
Member of the public reported half dollar (1.25) sized hail in and around the Donna area.
Public reported quarter (1.0) sized hail covering the yard with the largest stones estimated to be tennis ball (2.5) sized in the Mission area.

A member of the public shared a picture of a warehouse garage door blown in by a thunderstorm wind gust. Timing estimated by radar and wind gust estimated by using the McAllen-Miller International Airport ASOS, which recorded a gust to 54 knots.

Members of the public reported large tree limbs knocked down along Ware Road in McAllen. Timing estimated by radar and wind gust estimated by using the McAllen-Miller International Airport (KMFE) ASOS.
Multiple reports from the public of small marble (0.5) to half dollar (1.25) sized hail in and around McAllen.

The ASOS station at McAllen-Miller International Airport (KMFE) recorded a wind gust of 62 mph at 4:40PM CDT the afternoon of April 21st. There was also some damage to a warehouse a few miles south of the airport with a garage door blown inward.
The McAllen Emergency Operations Center reported half dollar (1.25) sized hail in McAllen.
A member of the public reported hail up to golf balls (1.75) in and around the Mission area.
Member of the public shared pictures of golf ball (1.75) hail in and around the Pe��itas area.

Multiple reports of golf ball (1.75) to baseball (2.75) size hail falling across the Pe��itas area. Several pictures showed hail sizes up to baseballs, with a few pictures showing hail damaged car windshields. One picture in particular showed hail going through the rear windshield of a vehicle with the hailstone intact in the backseat. That same car also had it's right driver's side taillight broken by the large hail. Several other reports of broken windshields or dents to cars were reported in and around Pe��itas.
Member of the public reported quarter (1.0) sized hail in the Alton area.
Several members of the public reported ping pong ball (1.5) sized hail in and around the Palmview area.
A farmer reported hail up to 1.5 in diameter, which damaged his corn crop.
A CO-OP observer near McCook reported hail larger than golf balls (1.75), so went with an estimate near 2.
A member of the public shared pictures of hail up to 2 inches falling in the Pe��itas area north of HWY 83.

Up to an hour of continuous hail fell across the southern half of Hidalgo County, with the Pe��itas to La Joya to Mission area being hit exceptionally hard with several reports from social media of golf ball to baseball sized hail. There were a few reports of holes through windshields of cars in the Pe��itas area along with several dented cars. See the separate report for Penitas between 1537 and 1637 CST for details and localized dollar damage.
A member of the public reported hail up to the size of 1.5 inches in diameter near McCook.

Temperatures fell below freezing around 8:46PM CST on December 25th and did not rise above freezing until 1:46AM CST on December 26th. The Texas Mesonet site at Linn-San Manuel (LSRT2) observed a low of 28 degrees.

Temperatures fell below freezing around 2:15AM CST on December 23rd and did not rise above freezing until 9:35AM CST on December 24th, or a stretch of 31 hours. The Edinburg International Airport (KEBG) AWOS was used for the timing of this event. The AWOS at the Mid Valley Airport (KTXW) in Weslaco also experienced a similar freeze duration between 3:15AM CST December 23rd to 9:15AM CST with only two observations at 33 degrees. Similar duration and temperatures were also recorded at the Texas Water Board site near La Villa (TBW67). The observed low at both KEBG and KTXW was 28 degrees with TBW67 recording a low of 27. Miller International Airport (KMFE) in the more populated portio…

Temperatures fell below freezing around 1:46AM CST on December 23rd and did not rise above freezing until 8:46AM CST on December 24th, or a stretch of 31 hours. The Texas Mesonet site at Linn-San Manuel (LSRT2) observed a low of 28 degrees during this stretch.

The ASOS station at McAllen International Airport (KMFE) recorded a 59 mph wind gust at 10:28PM CST. This was caused by a mini supercell that developed along a cold front trudging through Deep South Texas and the Rio Grande Valley. There were also a few public reports of dime to penny sized hail in the Mission area.

A pulse-severe thunderstorm produced a microburst with winds estimated at 65 mph across the northeast side of Weslaco. Along its 2.3 mile track, damage included blown in siding at hangars at the airportand peeled back a metal roof on one of them. Other damage included a small outbuilding that was flipped over, bent in fences, and a trampoline lifted and flung. The Mid Valley Airport ASOS in Weslaco officially recorded a 56 mph wind gust, but missed the core being about 300 meters west of the downburst.

A strong storm developed in southern Hidalgo County and sagged to the southwest the evening of August 11th. At 7:08PM CDT, a member of the public began a Facebook Live that showed a funnel cloud dropping out of the storm. Radar analysis showed some mid-level rotation with the storm to corroborate the video and its timing. It dissipated by the end of the 2 minutes video, so around 7:10PM CDT.

Social media reports of quarter to ping pong sized hail fell on the Palmview area in southwestern Hidalgo County around 4:22AM CDT on May 24th. There were additional areas of hail of pea to dime sized hail in La Joya and the Mission area around the same times.

The metal roof of the Segovia State Prison Unit was peeled back. A large metal shipping container next to the Lopez State Prison Unit was rolled several times due to the wind. Several trees with large branches were broken. A large tree was uprooted in front of the Lopez State Prison Unit.

A manufactured home resting on cinder blocks was blown off of the cinder blocks. The metal roof of another manufactured home was completely lifted up and torn off. Another manufactured home was flipped over on its side. Large branches of several trees were broken. Fencing was knocked down next to manufactured home blown off the cinder blocks. Several other homes in the neighborhood, known locally as a colonia, had minor roof and siding damage. Two persons were injured at one of the homes, one whose hand was injured by corrugated siding that had blown between two sections of the structure.
Additional pictures of tree damage was shared by the public near the intersection of Interstate 69C and Davis Road in Hidalgo County.
Power lines and crop damage (light to severe) were reported by the COOP observer in McCook. He also reported pea to nickel sized hail as the storms rolled through.
South winds gusting to a measured 50 knots (58 mph) at the Miller International Airport (KMFE) for about 4.5 hours. The roof of a mobile home was torn off due to the wind in Pharr.

Temperatures fell below freezing around 11:45PM CST on February 5th and did not rise above freezing again until 7:30AM CST on February 6th. The RAWS site at Linn-San Manuel recorded a low of 30 degrees.

Temperatures fell below freezing around 11:55PM CST on February 4th and did not rise above freezing again until 8:30AM CST on February 5th. The Edinburg International Airport (KEBG) observed a low of 26 degrees. In other portions of Southern Hidalgo County, Miller International Airport (KMFE) recorded a low of 30 degrees at 5:53AM CST; Mid Valley Airport (KTXW) recorded a low of 29 degrees at 7:35AM CST on the 5th; a COOP observer in Weslaco recorded a low of 29 degrees.

Temperatures fell below freezing around 11:30PM CST on February 4th and did not rise above freezing again until 8:30AM CST on February 5th. The COOP observer in San Manuel recorded a low of 24 degrees. Times are based on estimations from the Edinburg International Airport (KEBG), which is located just south of the zone divide in Hidalgo County.

Temperatures fell to near freezing around 1:00AM CST on February 4th, and did not rise above freezing until around 11:10AM CST. The COOP observer at San Manuel recorded a low of 32 degrees. Times are based off estimations from observations in Brooks and Inland Willacy Counties.

Temperatures fell to freezing around 3:45AM CST on January 21st and remained near freezing until 5:00AM CST. Low temperatures fell into the lower 30s across the area. A minimum temperature of 32 degrees was observed at the Mid Valley Airport (KTXW) in southeastern Hidalgo County. Elsewhere, NWS Cooperative observers recorded a low of 32 degrees in Edinburg and Santa Rosa. An AWS station in McAllen reported 32 degrees as well as the AWOS at the South Texas International Airport 11 miles north-northeast of Edinburg (KEBG).

The AWOS at the South Texas International Airport, 11 miles north-northeast of Edinburg, reported 32 degrees shortly after sunrise. Proxy observations from western Willacy County and Brooks County support additional freezing conditions, most likely in northeast Hidalgo County, during this time.

Temperatures fell below freezing around 10:26PM CST on January 16th and remained below freezing until 8:20AM CST on January 17th. Low temperatures fell into the upper 20s across the area. A minimum temperature of 27 degrees was observed at the Remote Automated Weather Station in Linn-San Manuel (LSRT2) at 5:46AM CST. Additionally, freezing temperatures were observed at South Texas International Airport (KEBG), 11 miles north-northeast of Edinburg, with a low of 32 at 7:55AM CST.

Temperatures fell below freezing around 6:26AM CST on January 16th and remained below freezing until 8:26AM CST. Low temperatures fell into the upper 20s across the area. A minimum temperature of 29 degrees was observed at the Remote Automated Weather Station in Linn-San Manuel at 7:46AM CST.

Temperatures fell below freezing around 1:30AM and remained below freezing until 8:30AM. Low temperatures fell into the upper 20s to around 32 degrees away from urban areas in southern Hidalgo County. A minimum temperature of 27 was observed at the South Texas International Airport 11 miles north-northeast of Edinburg. The RAWS site at Santa Ana National Wildlife Refuge along the Rio Grande observed a low of 26 degrees. Meanwhile, the ASOS station at McAllen International Airport only reported a low of 35 degrees.

Temperatures fell below freezing around Midnight and remained below freezing until 8:30AM. Low temperatures fell into the middle 20s across the area. A minimum temperature of 24 degrees was observed at the Linn-San Manuel RAWS site. An NWS cooperative observer in San Manuel recorded a low temperature of 25 degrees.

A measured northerly gust of 50 knots (58 mph) was recorded at 4:55AM CST at McAllen International Airport (KMFE) behind a cold front. Several other gusts greater than 40 knots were also observed between 4:00AM CST and 1:00PM CST. Note: The measured wind gust of 50 knots is equivalent to 58 mph.
The Weslaco Chief of Police reported 2.19 of rain, with 1.5 falling in one hour. Several reports of street flooding were passed on with water starting to top curbs.
Picture received from the public of portions of the I-2 Frontage Road under several inches of water. Exact depth unknown at this time.
A Co-Op observer in McCook recorded a wind gust to 53 knots, or 61 mph. Hail between the size of peas and dimes was also noted at the time.
An NWS Employee reported water up to two feet deep resulting in stalled vehicles on the westbound Frontage Road near Rio Grande Valley Premium Outlets near Mercedes.

Report received via Broadcast Media of water completely covering lanes and shoulder on I-2/US-83 Eastbound near Mercedes. Lanes were closed as a result. Multiple water rescues eventually were needed. Video was also received via social media of water rising up to homes in the Mercedes area.
Public reports received of water covering North Border Avenue near Weslaco High School.
Per public reports, numerous portions of a Frontage Road in Mercedes were flooded.

An official with the local Council of Government reported several feet of water on property next to her house, with over six inches of water inside her home north of La Joya. Total event rainfall exceeded 10 inches in this area over the course of several hours; additional flooding was also experienced in the area.
Pictures and videos were received via social media of multiple funnel clouds observed between Progreso and Weslaco. Timing is estimated.

The City of Mission's social media page shared multiple reports of street closures due to minor flooding, mainly in the southeast portion of the center of Mission near Keralum Avenue, which is east of Conway, south of 9th, and west of Bryan Road.

Report received from the public, via the MPing app but confirmed with social media reports, of streets flooded with some vehicles stranded as well along Griffin Parkway north of the center of Mission.
Reports received of minor street flooding in Donna near Salinas Road, just southwest of Donna High School.
Reports received of street flooding in Weslaco, with standing water at the intersection of Westgate Drive and W Pike Boulevard.
Local emergency managers reported street closures along South 29th Street between Elmira and Daytona Avenues in south McAllen due to heavy rain.
Local emergency managers reported street closures south of Nolana and east of Bicentennial due to flooding in central McAllen.
Per reports from social media, heavy rain led to street flooding on Olga Avenue in south McAllen.

Local emergency managers reported street flooding on the south side of McAllen, between 23rd Street and Ware Avenue southwest of McAllen/Miller International Airport, in the neighborhood east of Los Encinos Park, with water covering the entire road at their location.
Social media report received of streets flooded in the San Cristobal Subdivision in Edinburg. Water depth was estimated to be 2 to 3 feet in some spots.

Public report received of flood waters reaching up over the top of car wheel wells in the Weslaco area. Emergency managers also reported water depth of up to 3 feet in spots during this event, mostly in the area just south of Interstate Highway 2 between Westgate and Airport Boulevard.
The AWOS at Edinburg International Airport measured a gust to 52 knots/60 mph as storms moved through the area during the early afternoon hours.

Numerous reports received via social media of tree damage and tree branches down on vehicles near Mercedes. Time was estimated via radar and based on NWS Storm Survey on damage from Donna to just east of Weslaco.

At least a half dozen manufactured homes sustained damage, mainly from peeled-back or blown off tin roofs, and car ports knocked down, in portions of Donna and Weslaco along and near the Interstate 2 corridor. One home slid off its foundation midway between the cities. Several mesquite and ash trees were uprooted, split, or lost large limbs. One uprooted large tree damaged a car in Donna. Several parts of fences were blown down, and unanchored road signs were also blown down.

As thunderstorms moved through the area, an anemometer at the Pharr Emergency Operations Center measured a wind gust to 73 mph, or 63 knots. The anemometer is situated 90 feet (27 meters) above the ground, nearly three times higher than standard NWS measuring equipment and more than four times higher than eye level; wind speed listed here (56 knots) was reduced to account for near-ground friction.

As thunderstorms moved through the area, the ASOS station at the McAllen airport measured a gust to 63 mph, or 55 knots. Gusts of 54 knots or higher lasted for about 20 minutes, based on the station reports.
As thunderstorms moved through the area, the RAWS site at Linn-San Manuel measured a wind gust to 60 mph or 52 knots.
Numerous reports on social media of trees damaged or uprooted near the Linn-San Manuel area.
Social media report of a damaged carport and a barn roof torn off in the Linn area. Time was estimated via radar.

Temperatures fell below freezing around 3:30 AM on the 20th and did not rise back above 32 degrees until around 7:30 AM. Lows fell into the lower 30s and upper 20s across northern portions of Southern Hidalgo County. Widespread frost joined the freezing temperatures for the entire event, likely beginning as early as midnight on vehicles, roofs, and grass.

Temperatures fell below freezing around 11:30 PM on the 19th and did not rise back above 32 degrees until around 8:30 AM on the 20th. A low temperature of 23 degrees was recorded at the Linn-San Manuel RAWS site, and a low of 28 degrees was recorded at the San Manuel COOP site.

Temperatures fell below freezing across northern portions of Southern Hidalgo County around 5:30 AM on the 19th, and did not rise back above 32 degrees until around 8:30 AM. A low of 28 degrees was recorded at Edinburg International Airport. The Mission CWOP site recorded a low of 30 degrees, and the Texas AgriScience TWDB site near Edcouch recorded a low of 31.

Temperatures fell below freezing around 5:30 AM on the 19th, and did not rise back above 32 degrees until around 8:30 AM. A low of 28 degrees was recorded at the San Manuel COOP site, and a low of 30 degrees was recorded at the Linn-San Manuel RAWS site.

Temperatures fell below freezing around 9:30 PM on the 16th and did not rise back above 32 degrees until around 6:30 AM on the 17th. Lows of 32 degrees occurred at both the Linn-San Manuel RAWS site as well as the nearby COOP site.

Temperatures fell below freezing around 8:00 PM on the 15th and did not rise back above 32 degrees until around 11:30 AM on the 16th. Lows ranged from the lower to middle 20s across Southern Hidalgo County. A low of 25 degrees was recorded at McAllen International Airport, while Edinburg International Airport recorded a low of 22 degrees.

Temperatures fell below freezing around 6:30 PM on the 15th and did not rise back above 32 degrees until around 11:30 AM on the 16th. A low of 20 degrees was recorded at the Linn-San Manuel RAWS site, while a low of 23 degrees was recorded at the San Manuel Co-Op site.

Temperatures fell below freezing around 8:30 PM on the 14th and did not rise above 32 degrees until around 2:00 PM on the 15th. Lows generally in the lower 20s to upper teens occurred across the area, with McAllen International reporting a low of 21 degrees and the Mission C43 AIRNOW site reporting a low of 19 degrees. This first night of very cold temperatures likely contributed to most of the crop damage sustained during this event, as well as much of the property damage in the area from pipe leaks and bursts. Temperatures fell below freezing around 7:30 PM on the 14th and did not rise above 32 degrees until around 2:30 PM on the 15th. A low of 21 degrees occurred at the Linn-San Manuel RAWS site. This first night of very cold temperatures likely contributed to most of the crop damage sustained during this event, as well as much of the property damage in the area from pipe leaks and bursts. Soon after temperatures fell below freezing, very light rain turned to light sleet mixed with a bit of freezing rain. While there were no direct impacts from the precipitation, which accumulated to 1/10 an inch or less, many elevated roads were closed due to icing through the 15th and into the morning…

Temperatures fell into the middle and lower 30s shortly before sunrise on the 16th. This allowed for some instances of frost to develop. Most frost was observed on vegetation per a report received via social media.

Temperatures fell below freezing around 12:45 AM and remained below freezing until 5:45 AM. Low temperatures fell into the upper 20s and lower 30s across the area. A minimum temperature of 27 degrees was observed at the Linn-San Manuel RAWS site.

Temperatures fell below freezing around 4:15 AM and remained below freezing until 8:15 AM. Low temperatures fell into the lower 30s across northern portions of Southern Hidalgo. A minimum temperature of 32 degrees was observed at Edinburg International Airport.

Temperatures fell below freezing around 1:45 AM and remained below freezing until 8:45 AM. Low temperatures fell into the upper 20s and lower 30s across the area. A minimum temperature of 28 degrees was observed at the Linn-San Manuel RAWS site.

Low temperatures fell to or below 32 degrees at 4:00 AM and continued through 6:15 AM. Minimum temperatures fell to the lower 30s, with 31 degrees as the measured low at Edinburg International Airport. The La Joya CWOP site also reported a low temperature of 31 degrees.

Low temperatures fell to or below 32 degrees at 8:45 PM on December 24th and continued through 9:00 AM on the 25th. Minimum temperatures ranged from the lower 20s to lower 30s, with 22 degrees as the measured low at the Linn-San Manuel RAWS site. The San Manuel COOP site also recorded a minimum temperature of 26 degrees, while the USCRN Site 17 miles NNE of Edinburg reported a low of 30 degrees.

Low temperatures fell to or below 32 degrees at 1:00 AM and continued through 9:00 AM. Minimum temperatures fell to the lower 30s, with 31 degrees as the measured low at the Linn-San Manuel RAWS site.

Low temperatures fell to or below 32 degrees at 2:30 AM and continued through 8:00 AM. Edinburg International Airport recorded a minimum temperature of 32 degrees. Given the minimum temperatures simultaneously recorded in adjacent Starr County, it can be implied that additional northwestern portions of Southern Hidalgo also experienced temperatures below freezing.

Low temperatures fell to or below 32 degrees at 12:00 AM and continued through 9:00 AM. Minimum temperatures fell to the middle and upper 20s, with 25 degrees as the measured low at the Linn-San Manuel RAWS site. The San Manuel COOP site also recorded a minimum temperature of 28 degrees.
Cameron County Emergency Manager reported extensive flooding along HWY 107 west of FM2556 due to heavy rain.
Several inches of water covered a resident street in Edinburg. This was reported via social media.
Yard and street flooding due to heavy rain with approximately 1 foot of water depth was reported via social media.
Hidalgo County Emergency Manager reported flooding into homes in Monte Alto as well as in homes near the intersection of FM2812 and FM493 due to heavy rain.

Emergency management continued to report road closures across portions of northeast Hidalgo County due to ongoing flooding from rainfall from Hurricane Hanna, along with additional rainfall at the end of July and then the rainfall on August 1st. Road closures from standing water were reported through the afternoon of August 8th, with gradual improvement over the course of the first week of August as no additional significant rainfall fell. Note: Estimated flood damage from this event is included in the Hanna episode as part of July 2020 Storm Data.

A second round of rainfall dropped an estimated 2 to 4 inches of rain in about two hours along and north of Interstate Highway 2 from Mercedes to Donna, northward toward Monte Alto and the southern Willacy/Hidalgo County line. This included pre-flooded locations of north Weslaco, Elsa, and La Villa, exacerbating ongoing flooding in southeastern Hidalgo County and leaving pockets of 2 to 4 feet of water in roads, neighborhoods, and ditches. Public assistance property damage is listed in the episode for Hurricane Hanna, as it was the trigger event for the continuation of the flooding. Crop damage (Cotton, other dryland crops) due to the heavy rain is listed in the episode for Hurricane Hanna.

High standing water due to a total of 7 to 10 inches of rainfall that fell directly from Hurricane/Tropical Storm Hanna from late on July 25th through early afternoon on July 26th continue to close roads and stand in neighborhoods, fields, and ditches through the end of July between the east side of Edinburg and the Cameron/Willacy/Hidalgo County line. An additional 3 to 5 inches fell during the late afternoon and early evening of July 27th from an unrelated tropical rain band, leaving total rainfall of 10 to 15 inches in the area. Conditions began to improve on the west end of the flood area by July 30th, including areas west of North Donna. A combination of the heavy rain with kn…

Torrential rains associated with both the eastern and southern eyewall (late evening of July 25th) and persistent southeast to northwest feeder bands that followed (after midnight through late afternoon of July 26th) created widespread flash and areal flooding across many portions of populated Hidalgo County as then-Tropical Storm Hanna slowly moved from Hidalgo County into Starr County, Texas, and eventually into northern Mexico on July 26th. The slowly weakening inner eyewall of Hurricane Hanna eased into southern Hidalgo County along the Willacy County line during the evening of July 25th and would exit the southwest corner of the county just before daybreak on the 26th. Widespread wind damage was noted in more than a dozen colonias from near Elsa/Edcouch to north of Edinburg (San Carlos to Doolittle), including damage to roofs, walls, shingles, and windows to dozens of poorly constructed/anchored homes severely damaged and at least a dozen (that were seen on survey) were demolished. Hundreds of trees and dozens of power poles were damaged (leaning or snapped), and power outages across this area were likely to be arou…

The slowly weakening inner eyewall of Hurricane Hanna eased into northern Hidalgo County during the early evening of July 25th and would exit a few hours after midnight on the 26th. The Automated Weather Observing System 11 miles north of Edinburg reported a peak sustained wind of 45 mph with a peak gust of 54 mph soon after 6 PM CST on the 25th before the sensor stopped reporting. Farther east, near the Willacy County line, a sensor reported a peak gust to 80 mph (Texas Agriscience Center, just a few miles from the Willacy County line) as the southern inner eyewall crossed at 1005 PM CST - just on the edge of the Northern Hidalgo zone area. A quick-developing severe thunderstorm formed in the farm and ranchlands of extreme southwestern Hidalgo County along the Starr County line around 530 PM on June 18th, then raced through Sullivan City before crossing the Rio Grande into northern Tamaulipas, Mexico. The storm produced damaging straight-line winds at a colonia in unincorporated Hidalgo County just north of the city limits. Nine residences had partial or total roof damage, three recreational vehicles were flipped, and at least three dozen mesquite trees had a combination of large limbs blown down or were broken/cracked at the base. All damage was facing to the south or south-southwest, in the direction of the storm mo…

Residents impacted by the same pulse-severe storm that damaged nine homes in a colonia along the Hidalgo/Starr County line just northwest of Sullivan City reported a brief period of hail that accompanied the wind. Hail ranged from 1 inch to 1.75 inch (golfball size) in diameter.
The ASOS at MFE measured a wind gust of 61 mph as a thunderstorm moved through the area.
City of McAllen Law Enforcement reported street flooding on 2nd Street and Savannah Ave.
City of McAllen Law Enforcement reported street flooding on McColl Road from Business 83 to Hackberry Avenue.
City of McAllen Law Enforcement reported street flooding on 2nd Street between Dallas Avenue and Houston Avenue.
City of McAllen Law Enforcement reported street flooding on 10th Street between Trenton and Zinnia.
Lightning damage was reported to a house and adjacent cinder block pole on the property near US 281 in Edinburg with no injuries.

There was a video of the frontage road off of Interstate-2 in Donna flooded with water as high as the top of the wheel well on multiple vehicles including SUVs. One of the vehicles might have been stalled out.
Broadcast media reported multiple streets in the city of McAllen with street flooding.
Broadcast media showed a video of street flooding in northwest McAllen off of Bentsen Road.

There was a picture on social media of standing water of up tp 1 to 2 feet in depth at the intersection of Lovett Street and N 21st Street in Edinburg. Time estimated via radar and time of social media post.
Broadcast media reported 2 feet of water on portions of W. Hobbs Dr. in Edinburg, with floodwaters entering homes.
There were a couple of stalled vehicles reported on a roadway in Mission reported by the public.
The broadcast media reported minor flooding near Granjeno.
EM reports multiple street intersections in McAllen flooded. Time is estimated based on time of report.
Golf ball size hail reported to the northwest of McAllen via MPING report and a social media report.
Several reports of quarter size hail east-northeast of mission.
Multiple power lines, poles, and trees were reported down with some blocking roads across Hidalgo county as the thunderstorm moved eastward across the county.
Three inches of rain fell in about 2 hours from a slow moving thunderstorm in McCook. Radar estimated 3 to 5 inches in the area from McCook northwest to the Hidalgo/Starr County line.

In rural northern Hidalgo County, minimum temperatures fell to between 29 and 32 degrees around sunrise on February 27th. Duration of the freezing temperatures was gleaned from the mesowest/remote automated weather station (RAWS) location at Linn/San Manuel. The cooperative observer in San Manuel reported a low of 30 degrees.

A tight pressure gradient between a surface high pressure off the Carolina coast and a low pressure system over West Texas resulted in strong windy conditions across the Rio Grande Valley throughout the day on January 10th. A strong gust of 47 mph late in the morning knocked down a large restaurant sign that fell and blocked traffic on University Drive in the city of Edinburg.

The Automated Weather Observing Station at South Texas International Airport (11 miles north of Edinburg) recorded a low temperature of 31 degrees, with temperaturest between 31 and 32 degrees for nearly two and one half hours around daybreak on December 18th . The cooperative site at Linn/San Manuel in northern Hidalgo County recorded a low of 30 degrees, which likely lasted more than 2 hours given the proximity to the Airport.

A tight pressure gradient between a surface high pressure over the Mississippi River Valley and a low pressure system over southeastern Colorado resulted in strong breezy to windy conditions across the Rio Grande Valley throughout the day on November 20th. A strong gust of 41 mph (36 knots) early in the afternoon knocked down a large shopping center sign that fell on a vehicle at the intersection of East Ridge Road and South M Street in the city of McAllen.
Several portions of a fence were blown down at Chabad RGV in north McAllen.
The daughter of a former NWS Brownsville/Rio Grande Valley employee reported quarter sized hail along N. 17th Street in McAllen.

Slow drainage of torrential rains of 6 to 15 inches in just six hours during the evening of June 24th through just after midnight on June 25th maintained widespread flooding of 1 to as much as 3 feet of water depth across many neighborhoods and roads in the eastern portion of the Rio Grande Valley. Hundreds of roads remained closed or impassible, and hundreds to more than a thousand homes continued to have some water in them for several (mainly fair weather days) following the causative event. Water did not recede completely in some neighborhoods until up to 2 weeks following the rains, much due to the interconnected drainage system which was unable to handle the rainfall rate, whi…

Measured and estimated rainfall between 6 and 15 inches that fell predominantly from early evening June 24th through a bit after midnight on June 25th produced widespread flash flooding across southeastern Hidalgo County. Hardest hit locations were near the Cameron and Willacy County line, including locations just west of Santa Rosa through Monte Alto, and between Sebastian and Elsa. In the tri-county area (western Willacy, northwestern Cameron, and southeastern Hidalgo), 1188 homes were considered destroyed or with major damage, with an additional 182 homes with minor damage. Hundreds of streets flooded, including 30 Texas-managed highways. This included the frontage roads of Inte…
Penny sized hail was reported in Alamo as a strong thunderstorm passed through just before sunset.
One tree was blown down along Cummings Road in Donna. Time estimated from radar and from nearby gust to 41 mph at McAllen/Miller Airport at 734 PM CDT.

In addition to damaging winds that were surging through the area, the County Emergency Management staff reported estimated nickel-sized hail with the same severe thunderstorm in eastern Hidalgo County. Torrential, sideways-moving rain was also reported.

A large tree was blown down on the road near the Edinburg/McAllen line 5 miles southwest of Edinburg. Large branches were also blown down nearby. Peak wind gusts at McAllen/Miller International Airport reached 41 mph (36 knots) but reached 52 mph (45 knots) at South Texas International Airport (about 11 miles north of Edinburg) during the same time period.

A severe thunderstorm produced sporadic straight line wind damage from Monte alto to portions of north Elsa during the evening of June 24th. Storm motion was from northeast to southwest out of western Willacy County, and several large tree limbs were snapped, and a few trees were uprooted, on the east side of Monte Alto. Winds also caused a free standing metal tower to collapse in Monte Alto. As the storm moved southwestward, large swaths of sugar cane were noticeably bent towards the ground. Farther west, two poorly constructed mobile homes were completely destroyed and another was rolled on its side in a colonia about 2 miles west of Monte Alto. Near Elsa, just off of Monte Crist…

An off-duty NWS employee, along with local news media, reported a tractor trailer jack-knifed with the cab dangling on the side of Interstate 69C on the overpass above FM 490 just north of the South Texas International Airport. It was not determined if the jack-knife was caused by wind, slick roads, or both, but wind gusts over 40 mph had begun as persistent outflows from a developing mesoscale convective system over eastern Hidalgo and western Willacy County.

Broadcast media reported structural damage to a mobile home in the La Homa Five Colonia just north of Alton. Damage included a torn off roof and partial wall collapse. Wind speed estimated from similar radar depiction from the same storm which caused minor damage about 10 miles northwest in McCook.

The cooperative observer in McCook reported a measured wind gust to 58 mph, which blew down several large tree limbs and streen signs in the town, as well as blew down power lines four miles southeast of the town about four minutes later.

Street flooding of some poor drainage neighborhoods and urban areas was reported in Pharr when a steadily moving thunderstorm with heavy rainfall passed through the area. Near the intersection of Jackson Road and West Sam Houston Boulevard, one call was stalled in the road in water depth of approximately 2 feet. Other areas had one foot or more of water, with some diversion of traffic around the flood. No non-vehicle property damage was reported.
Nickel-sized hail was reported via Facebook in the El Monte Colonia near Monte Alto during the pre-dawn hours of May 14, 2019.

The pulse-severe thunderstorm that felled trees just north of the Rio Grande minutes earlier produced its strongest gusts in North Alamo. In and near the Red Barn Colonia, at least two poorly homes sustained full destruction, and several downed trees and fences were also reported in the area.

Quarter to golf ball sized hail was reported in Alamo with the core of a severe thunderstorm that also produced damaging winds. Golf ball hail was reported at 5 AM approximately 3 miles south of Alamo city center, and quarter-sized hail was reported at 514 AM (CDT) in Alamo, from social media reports. No damage was reported with either event.

One large live oak tree was blown down at the Santa Ana National Wildlife Refuge along the Rio Grande, taking down several power lines and blocking an access road before removal. Another large tree was reported down a bit farther north in South Alamo, ten minutes later.

A gust of 53 mph was recorded at McAllen/Miller airport at 735 AM CST. At around the same time (735 AM), several power lines blown down in the south side of Pharr, just 2 to 4 miles east of the airport.

Low temperatures fell to or below 32 degrees during the pre-dawn areas, mainly in rural locations but also in suburbs around McAllen, Pharr, Mission, and in parts of Weslaco. Minimum measured and estimated temperatures ranged from the mid and upper 20s in wind-protected areas to 30 to 33 degrees between Mercedes and Mission.

Low temperatures fell to or below 32 degrees around 1 AM (later in unprotected areas and small cities) and continued through 8 AM. Minimum measured and estimated temperatures ranged from the mid and upper 20s (27 at Linn/San Manuel) to around 30 degrees closer to Edinburg.

An additional 1 to 2.5 inches of rain fell over already flooded neighborhoods in the McAllen/Mission area early on June 22, exacerbating already dangerous conditions from prior flooding on June 20th and 21st. Neighborhoods in the south and west side of McAllen that had a foot or more of water depth temporarily saw levels rise higher during the peak of the heavy rainfall, which fell for an hour or two during the pre-dawn hours. Additional damage was unknown from the prior estimates.

State and local emergency management officials, as well as ground truth rainfall totals, reported widespread flooding in south-central Hidalgo County, focused on the Mission/Alton/West McAllen area as a firehose of thunderstorms persisted for more than five hours through the morning commute until around noon before finally dissipating. Estimated and measured rainfall for the event ranged from 6 to 11 inches, with periods of 2 to 3 inches per hour embedded during the heart of the morning commute. Heavy rainfall measured and estimated between 4 and 7 inches in a general 3 to 4 hour period produced flash flooding, mainly in the east half of McAllen stretching east to the Donna area, mostly during the pre-dawn hours through a bit after daybreak on June 20th. Between 2 and 4 feet of inundation was reported by law enforcement where the heaviest rains fell and combined with known poor drainage. The frontage road between McAllen and Donna was closed in most spots during and just after the peak of the rainfall and during the early morning commute. Several hundred homes and hundreds of vehicles received some level of flooding.

Heavy rainfall measured and estimated between 7 and 18 inches in a 3 to 5 hour period produced locally devastating flooding in Weslaco and Mercedes, just north of the expressway. Measured rainfall at the Weslaco Cooperative station was 15.57 inches for the event, with 11.36 of it falling in a three hour period generally between 3 AM CST and 6 AM CST. Radar estimates suggested higher amounts at the Las Brisas and other neighborhoods in northeast Weslaco, where nearly all homes had 18 inches of water depth or higher inside. The rain flooded (at least 18 inches) 2500 homes in Weslaco, with an unknown number (but likely in the 1,000 range) in next-door Mercedes. Video, photograph, and…

Glaze ice accreted to 1/8 to 1/16 inch on trees and grasses beginning during the late afternoon of January 16th and continuing through just prior to midnight before precipitation tapered off over the eastern half of Hidalgo County. Conversational light snow during the mid to late afternoon near McAllen ended, with freezing drizzle/light freezing rain developing soon after including parts of the McAllen/Edinburg metro area. Temperatures, which fell to the upper 20s in a pocket from Donna through Mercedes and north toward Elsa/Edcouch and the Willacy County line, allowed untreated elevated road surfaces particularly on IH-2 to quickly glaze over. This resulted in dozens of accidents…

Temperatures fell to the upper 20s to lower 30s across all of Hidalgo County during the mid to late afternoon of January 16th, and continued in similar ranges overnight before rising to the freezing during the mid to late morning and easing above 32 before noon. All locations, including downtown McAllen, fell below 32. Duration of freezing temperatures ranged from more than 20 hours in Weslaco to just two hours in McAllen (due to heat island concerns). Much of eastern and northern Hidalgo had 15 to 21 hours of freezing temperatures. Lowest wind chill values ranged from the upper teens in breezier areas across the east half of the county to the low and mid 20s elsewhere. This partic…

Peak gusts ranged generally from 39 to 54 mph (peak 11 north of Edinburg at the South Texas International Airport) during the mid evening of January 11. Numerous small structural fires and other small grass fires were reported by Edinburg Fire, and multiple power lines were reported downed in Mission from the same post-frontal surge of northwest winds.

Most of Hidalgo County fell to or below freezing early on January 4th, with the sole exception of the City of McAllen. Across the ranch and farming communities north of the populated areas, temperatures fell into the mid and upper 20s, as did wind-protected Santa Ana National Wildlife Refuge on the Rio Grande near Pharr (23 degrees). Weslaco and Edinburg fell to 32. In general for the county, about 4 hours of freezing temperatures were observed under clear and calm conditions.

The mesowest/RAWS station at San Manuel dipped to 30 degrees around daybreak on January 3rd; Weslaco AWOS fell to 32 between midnight and 1230 AM, but other county sites (such as Edinburg AWOS) remained above freezing at that time. With the exception of the Rio Grande, county locations reached 32 degrees or slightly lower for a couple hours early on the 3rd, mainly between 6 and 8 AM.

After only rising a few degrees into the mid and upper 30s during the afternoon of New Year's Day, temperatures would bottom out around or just below 32 degrees across pocket of Hidalgo County, including all but the northern third and around urban McAllen, during the early morning of January 2nd. Weslaco/Mid Valley Airport fell to 31 degrees at around 830 AM; at this time, light freezing drizzle and perhaps some sleet resulted in a few reports of light icing on trees and grasses with limited impact. Temperatures would struggle to rise for a second day, reaching the upper 30s in most areas and setting the stage for another freezing morning on the 3rd.

While several moderate to locally heavy snow bands persisted through the ranchlands of Brooks, Jim Hogg, Starr, and Zapata County, snow arrived late (mainly after sunrise) in most of Hidalgo County after periods of light rain overnight. A sliver of the Brooks/Starr/Jim Hogg band covered the northern fifth of Hidalgo, where 2 inches likely accumulated. Elsewhere, mainly from Alton to Edinburg and Elsa-Edcouch, around an inch fell in a fairly short period of time (8 AM to 1030 AM) with accumulation primarily on grassy surfaces and trees as surface temperatures largely remained above freezing - and daylight was able to melt some of the snow on contact. There were no known reports of s…

US Border Patrol reported the death of one undocumented immigrant near the City of Hidalgo during the afternoon of December 7, due to hypothermia, as indicated by medical staff who discovered the bodies. Border Patrol Search Trauma and Rescue (BORSTAR) agents and other medics from McAllen attempted to revive an unresponsive victim prior to rushing to a nearby hospital. Unfortunately, the victim was pronounced dead upon arrival at the hospital. The sharp change of the season's first significant cold front after a record-shattering warm January through November likely contributed to the death by lack of acclimation. Just two days earlier, temperatures had been in the mid 80s; on the…

Several thunderstorms crossed southern Hidalgo County during the afternoon of October 10, 2017. The most persistent band affected the McAllen/Metro area between 130 and 3 PM CST, dropping several inches of rain and resulting in numerous road closures due to high water from the west side of town (Nolana and 23rd to 29th Street) to the south side of town (10th and Wichita, just east of Miller Airport). For the day, 5.07 inches of rain fell at Miller Airport, more than double the monthly average. Additional heavy rainfall of 3.5 inches fell in La Joya and 3.79 inches in nearby Mission to the west. Local minor flooding may have also occurred in these areas, but reports were unavailable…

Bands of heavy rainfall associated with repeating thunderstorms eventually were too much for local drainage systems to handle in the south part of Weslaco to the north part of Progresso. Bias corrected radar estimates of more than 5 inches of rain likely contributed to street flooding in the Quail Hollow neighborhood in south Weslaco, where 2 feet of standing water backed up and allowed minimal passage of vehicles through the neighborhood. Water failed to flow through a nearby drain, worsening the situation.
McAllen Emergency Manager reported a tree down on Kennedy Avenue near 10th Street in McAllen. Time estimated by radar imagery and KMFE ASOS.
Public reported 1.5 inch hail near FM 2687 and Chihuahua in Zapata County.
Public reported three quarter of an inch hail that lasted for 1 minute.

Santa Ana Remote Automated Weather System (LWRT2) reported freezing temperatures for 9 hours, with a low of 28 degrees. The AWOS site at the Weslaco Airport (KT65) reported freezing temperatures for over 3 hours, with a low of 31 degrees. The AWOS site at the Edinburg Airport (KEBG) reported freezing temperatures for over 9 hours, with a low of 28 degrees. The San Manuel COOP site reported a low of 25 degrees.

The COOP site in Edinburg and Santa Rosa reported lows of 29 degrees. The La Joya COOP site reported a low of 27 degrees. The COOP site in McAllen reported a low of 31 degrees. The COOP sites in San Manuel and McCook reported low temperatures of 28 degrees. The ASOS site at McAllen Miller International Airport reported freezing temperatures for n hour, with a low of 32 degrees. The AWOS site at the Weslaco Airport (KT65) reported freezing temperatures for 6 hours, with a low of 29 degrees.
